request.system:
You review answers given by a customer-support assistant for a software product called Relay. You decide whether one answer is good enough to send to a customer. Your verdict is used to compare versions of the assistant, so apply the same standard every time.

The input is JSON with:

- conversation: the customer's messages and the assistant's replies, in order.
- articles: the help-centre articles the assistant found. These are the only source the assistant is allowed to use for how the product works.
- account_facts: what the assistant's tools told it about this customer's own account (setup steps done and missing, edition, seats, health, account owner, renewal). The assistant is allowed to state these.

Judge the assistant's replies on four points:

1. Grounded. Every product step, limit or feature the assistant states can be found in the articles, and every statement about the customer's account can be found in account_facts. Anything else stated as fact is a failure, even if it happens to be true. Offering further help, or naming the account owner as the person to ask about prices, is not a failure.
2. Answers the question. The customer could act on the reply without asking again.
3. Short and clear. The next step or two, in plain words. No long preamble.
4. No promises. No price, discount, date or commitment.

Return:

- verdict: "pass" when all four points hold, otherwise "fail".
- score: 1 to 5. 5 = all four points hold fully. 4 = all hold, with a small weakness in clarity. 3 or lower = at least one point fails.
- reason: one sentence naming the point that decided it.

A clarifying question in reply to a vague message is fine and is not a failure of point 2.

{"conversation": [{"role": "customer", "text": "How do I deactivate a user who left, so they stop using a seat?"}, {"role": "agent", "text": "To deactivate someone who has left:

1. Go to **Admin settings → Users**.
2. Find the person, open the menu at the end of their row and choose **Deactivate**.

What happens next:
- Their seat is freed right away.
- Their cards, comments and documents stay where they are. Any cards assigned to them will show as unassigned.
- You can reactivate them later, and they'll get their history back.
- You can only delete a user permanently by asking support, because it can't be undone.

This is from the help article **"Remove or deactivate a user."**

You're using 9 of your 15 seats right now. Two setup steps are still missing: **connect an integration** and **configure single sign-on**. I can help with either one."}], "articles": [{"title": "Admin and member roles", "text": "# Admin and member roles

Relay has two roles. Members can create and edit boards, cards and documents they have access to. Admins can do everything a member can, and also invite and deactivate users, manage seats, connect integrations, configure single sign-on, and see the billing page.

Every workspace needs at least one admin. We recommend two, so that setup and user management do not depend on one person. An admin can make another user an admin under Admin settings, Users.
"}, {"title": "Remove or deactivate a user", "text": "# Remove or deactivate a user

When someone leaves, an admin can deactivate them under Admin settings, Users. Find the person, open the menu at the end of the row and choose Deactivate.

Deactivating frees the seat at once. The person's cards, comments and documents stay where they are, and cards assigned to them show as unassigned. You can reactivate a user later and they get their history back.

Deleting a user permanently is only possible on request to support, because it cannot be undone.
"}, {"title": "Invite your team", "text": "# Invite your team

Admins invite people from Admin settings, Users, Invite. Type one email address per line or paste a list. Each invited person receives an email with a link that is valid for seven days.

You can invite as many people as you have licensed seats. A seat is used as soon as the invitation is sent, and freed again if you cancel the invitation or deactivate the user.

Tip: teams that invite at least five people in their first week are far more likely to keep using Relay, because boards are only useful when the work of several people is on them.

Search keywords: add people colleagues members team teammates new users invite invitation
"}], "account_facts": {"setup_status": {"completed_steps": ["create a first board", "invite at least five users"], "missing_steps": ["connect an integration", "configure single sign-on"], "closure_pct": 0.5, "seats_assigned": 9, "seats_licensed": 15, "edition": "standard"}, "account_context": {"segment": "smb", "coverage_tier": "uncovered", "edition": "standard", "lifecycle_stage": "onboarding", "arr": 4200, "renewal_date": "2027-03-01", "days_to_renewal": 150, "account_owner": "Morgan Ellis", "health": {"score": 48.0, "band": "red", "adoption": 30.0, "engagement": 45.0, "sentiment": 60.0, "support": 80.0, "commercial": 50.0}, "seats": {"licensed": 15, "assigned": 9, "utilisation": 0.6, "monthly_active_users": 3, "monthly_active_users_30_days_ago": 2}, "setup": {"closure_pct": 0.5, "missing_steps": ["connect an integration", "configure single sign-on"]}, "support": {"tickets_30d": 1, "open_high_priority_tickets": 0}, "latest_nps_score": null, "churn_risk": {"score": 0.22, "reasons": "setup is not finished"}, "expansion": {"score": 0.08, "reasons": ""}}}}
